## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials in this search yet. The earlier 84 trials all scored 0 on dev and on training, so the agent never completed an exact build. That points to optimisation and inductive bias, not generalisation. None of the families listed in the program gives evidence for any idea, and I expect the starting architecture to score 0 again. This round therefore tries six untested combinations that differ substantially from one another. Each stacks orthogonal initialisation, near-uniform starting policy logits, value-layer gain 1, normalisation in the trunk, a learned 1x1 skip from the raw observation into the placement head, and a factorised logit (shared anchor term + per-type bias + per-type interaction). The candidates differ in three ways: (1) how the head combines footprint cells (pooling, a learned conv over the footprint, bilinear or gated AND-like interactions, per-layer grouped features), (2) whether weights are shared across brick types, and (3) the recipe (more updates, 1 epoch with long rollouts, gamma 0.99–0.995). Any score above 0 is a signal to follow in later rounds.

### Round 2
All six round-1 stacks scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, like the 84 earlier trials. Each one combined init hygiene, GroupNorm, a raw skip, factorised logits and recipe changes on top of a pooled-projection footprint head. So the agent still never finishes an exact build. That points to optimisation and inductive bias, not generalisation. A placement is correct when every footprint cell has the same next target layer and at least one cell is directly supported. That is an AND/OR over per-cell boolean features. Linear projections that are then min- or max-pooled express this poorly. Sigmoid per-cell features that are then min-pooled (AND) and max-pooled (OR) express it directly. None of this has been tested. Round 2 stacks that head with: deep per-cell MLPs; window convs that see which cell is which, plus context; row and column context; a lean net trained for 1 epoch to get the most samples; a sharp recipe; and a myopic recipe. Every candidate changes a lot at once.

### Round 3
All 12 trials score 0 on dev and on training success. That covers AND/OR sigmoid heads, window convs, GLU, layer-grouped heads, gamma 0.9 to 0.995, and 1 to 4 epochs, so no idea has evidence yet. One hypothesis fits every failure. The per-placement reward charges only 1/N for an extra cell, so a big brick that is 3/4 correct still beats a correct 1x1, especially at low gamma. PPO then settles on fast, sloppy filling. It never sees the +1 exact-build bonus, and greedy evaluation picks the sloppy big brick. Precision only pays when gamma is near 1, where an extra cell costs about 1/N - 0.02 net. So this round leans toward gamma 0.995 with moderate lambda and low entropy, across several architectures. It also adds untested items: coordinate channels, a dense head next to the footprint head, a type-then-anchor softmax with a learned temperature, many small 1-epoch updates, and heavy sample reuse.

### Round 4
All 18 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, the same as the starting architecture. The recipes ranged from 1 to 6 PPO epochs, 88k to 426k steps, gamma 0.9 to 0.995 and clip 0.1 to 0.3. The architectures included pooled, window, bilinear, gated and layer-grouped footprint heads, dense heads, a type-then-anchor softmax and init hygiene. Because training success is also 0, the agent never completes an exact build even with a stochastic policy, so this is an optimisation or perception failure, not a generalisation one. No result separates any idea from another. This is the last round, so I am spreading the 6 slots over untested directions rather than refining anything:
- more trunk depth with clip 0.3;
- learned anchor remapping, in case the world's action layout differs from the description;
- large low-noise batches at the highest learning rate;
- a DONE logit driven by a learned per-cell detector of remaining cells;
- periodic height features, so the net can compare build and target heights;
- a fourth "everything plausible" stack.
